wordings.TRANSFORMER_DESCRIPTION: The encoder-decoder transformer of Vaswani et al. (2017), in the base size of Table 3. The encoder reads a sentence in the source language and writes one vector per source position. The decoder reads those vectors together with a sentence in the target language and returns, at every target position, the probability of every token of the vocabulary. Attention and feed-forward layers make up the whole model, with no recurrence and no convolution.
wordings.INPUT_EMBEDDING_DESCRIPTION: The source sentence X arrives as x token identifiers, one for each position of the sentence. $EMBEDDING_SENTENCE $SUM_DROPOUT_SENTENCE
wordings.OUTPUT_EMBEDDING_DESCRIPTION: The target sentence Y arrives as y token identifiers. During training it is the translation the decoder learns to reproduce, shifted right by one position so that position i holds the token before the one predicted there. During generation it holds the tokens generated so far. $EMBEDDING_SENTENCE $SUM_DROPOUT_SENTENCE
wordings.EMBEDDING_SENTENCE: The embedding E holds one learned vector of m values for every token of the vocabulary, and m, the model width, is the width of every vector the model passes between its layers. The source and the target share one vocabulary of byte-pair tokens, and the paper shares one weight matrix between the two embeddings and the output projection. The embedded vector is multiplied by the square root of m.
wordings.SUM_DROPOUT_SENTENCE: The positional encoding is added to the embedded vectors, and dropout is applied to the sum.
wordings.POSITIONAL_ENCODING_DESCRIPTION: Permuting the positions of the input of a self-attention permutes its outputs the same way and changes nothing else, so attention alone cannot tell where a token stands. The position of each token is therefore added to its embedding as a fixed pattern of sines and cosines. Channel 2i of the vector at a position holds the sine of an angle and channel 2i + 1 holds the cosine of the same angle, where the angle is the position times a frequency. The frequency of pair i falls geometrically from 1 at pair 0 towards 1/beta at the last pair, with beta = 10000. The table PE holds e raised to i times the angle, for every position and pair, which is the table a rotary embedding multiplies by. The imaginary unit times its conjugate is the sine plus the imaginary unit times the cosine, and writing each complex number as two channels, the real part first, puts the sine at channel 2i and the cosine at channel 2i + 1.
wordings.SELF_ATTENTION_DESCRIPTION: Every source position attends to every source position. $HEADS_SENTENCE The keys and the values are projected from the same copy of the source as the queries, so the scores relate every query position to every key position.
wordings.MASKED_SELF_ATTENTION_DESCRIPTION: Every target position attends to itself and to the target positions before it. $HEADS_SENTENCE $MASK_SENTENCE
wordings.CROSS_ATTENTION_DESCRIPTION: Every target position attends to every source position. The layer grabs the encoded input A from the tape, and every one of the N decoder layers reads the same A. The queries come from the target positions and the keys and the values from the encoded input, so information from the source sentence enters each decoder layer again. $HEADS_SENTENCE
wordings.HEADS_SENTENCE: Each of the h heads projects every position into a query, a key and a value of k values, and the heads compute scaled dot-product attention in parallel. The outputs of the heads are laid side by side, which the paper calls the concatenation, and the projection W^O maps the h times k values of each position back to m.
wordings.MASK_SENTENCE: During training the decoder reads the whole target sentence at once, so each position must be kept from reading the later positions, which hold the tokens it is trained to predict. The positions each query reads are chosen by the view named Mask, whose slot w of position y holds position y - w. A slot past the start of the sentence reads the unit, which the softmax and the weighted sum ignore.
wordings.CORE_DESCRIPTION: Each query takes the dot product with every key it reads, the scores are divided by the square root of the head width k, and a softmax over the keys turns the scores into weights that are positive and sum to one. Each query returns the sum of the values under those weights. Without the division the dot products grow with k, and a softmax of large scores has small gradients (Section 3.2.1).
wordings.FEED_FORWARD_DESCRIPTION: Two fully connected layers with a rectified linear unit between them, applied to every position on its own with the same weights. The first maps the m values of a position to f values, and the second maps them back to m. The inner width f is 2048 in the base model, four times the model width.
wordings.ADD_NORM_DESCRIPTION: A residual connection adds the output of the sublayer to the input of the sublayer. The sublayer therefore learns a change to its input, and its input passes through the stack unchanged when the change is zero. Dropout is applied to the output of the sublayer before the addition, and a layer normalisation follows the addition (Sections 3.1 and 5.4). The normalisation after the addition is the arrangement of the paper, and later transformers normalise the input of the sublayer instead.
wordings.ENCODER_DESCRIPTION: N = 6 encoder layers applied one after another, each with weights of its own. Each layer lets every source position read every other through self-attention and then transforms every position on its own through the feed-forward layer. The output of the last layer is the encoded input A, which the decoder uses to generate its output.
wordings.DECODER_DESCRIPTION: N = 6 decoder layers applied one after another, each with weights of its own. Each layer lets every target position read the positions before it through masked self-attention, reads the encoded input A through cross-attention, and transforms every position on its own through the feed-forward layer. The encoded input carries the source sentence. The target carries the translation to reproduce during training, or the tokens generated so far during generation.
wordings.OUTPUT_DESCRIPTION: A linear map takes the m values of every target position to one score for every token of the vocabulary, and a softmax over the vocabulary turns the scores into the probability of each token at that position (Section 3.4).
wordings.DROPOUT_DESCRIPTION: During training, dropout sets each value to zero with probability P_drop and divides every value it keeps by 1 - P_drop, so the expected value of each output equals its input. At inference it returns its input unchanged. A model trained with dropout cannot depend on any one value being present. The base model uses P_drop = 0.1 (Section 5.4).
wordings.EMBEDDING_OPERATOR_DESCRIPTION: A table lookup. The embedding holds one learned vector of m values for every token of the vocabulary, and it returns the vector of the token each position holds.
wordings.DECOMPLEX_DESCRIPTION: Each complex number written as two adjacent real values, the real part first, so that the t pairs of a position become its m = 2t channels.
wordings.QUERY_ROLE: The query projection of every head. Each position is projected into h queries of k values (Section 3.2.2).
wordings.KEY_ROLE: The key projection of every head. Each key position is projected into h keys of k values (Section 3.2.2).
wordings.VALUE_ROLE: The value projection of every head. Each key position is projected into h values of k values (Section 3.2.2).
wordings.OUTPUT_ROLE: The output projection, which maps the h heads of k values of each position back to the m values of the model width (Section 3.2.2).
wordings.FIRST_FEED_FORWARD_ROLE: The first layer of the feed-forward network, from the m values of a position to f values, with a bias (Section 3.3).
wordings.SECOND_FEED_FORWARD_ROLE: The second layer of the feed-forward network, from f values back to m, with a bias (Section 3.3).
wordings.OUTPUT_PROJECTION_ROLE: The pre-softmax linear map, which gives every target position one score per token of the vocabulary. The paper shares its weight with the two embeddings (Section 3.4).
wordings.LAYER_NORM_ROLE: For each position, the layer normalisation subtracts the mean of its m values and divides by their standard deviation, so the values of the position have a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Each of the m channels is then multiplied by a learned gain and has a learned bias added.
wordings.POSITIONAL_TABLE_ROLE: The table of the positional encoding. The angle of pair i at a position is the position times beta^(-i/t), with beta = 10000 and t = m / 2 pairs, which is the angle pos / 10000^(2i/m) of Section 3.5.
wordings.EMBEDDING_SCALE_ROLE: The embedded vector multiplied by the square root of the model width m (Section 3.4).
wordings.SCORE_SCALE_ROLE: Every score divided by the square root of the head width k (Section 3.2.1).
wordings.RELU_ROLE: The rectified linear unit, applied to every value on its own. It returns the value where the value is positive and zero elsewhere. Without a non-linear map between them, the two linear layers would compose into one linear map.
wordings.SINE_FIRST_ROLE: The imaginary unit times the conjugate of every entry of the table, which turns cos + i sin into sin + i cos, so the sine is the real part.
wordings.MASK_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Slot w of target position y reads position y - w of the array the view is applied to, so slot 0 is the position itself and slot w is the position w before it. A slot past the start of the sentence names a negative position, and a read outside an axis holds the unit, which the softmax and the weighted sum ignore. Each target position therefore reads itself and the positions before it and never a later one, which is the mask of Section 3.2.3. The slot axis leaves the view as w|y, which records that slot w holds a value where y - w is at least 0.
